detected_features.summary: OpenShell is explicitly single-player mode. Multi-tenancy requires namespace-scoped sandbox creation, owner/tenant labeling in gateway persistence, tenant-scoped provider isolation, RBAC authorization per tenant, and Helm chart namespace provisioning. Kagenti implements gateway-per-tenant pattern with Keycloak audience scoping. The #1722 issue has 5 reactions — highest on any open feature request.

detected_features.summary: OpenShell has no K8s operator. The gateway manages sandboxes directly through its compute driver with no CRD-based agent lifecycle management or operator reconciliation. Kagenti's AgentRuntime CRD + operator pattern provides declarative agent management. Building a Rust K8s operator with kube-rs is feasible but substantial — kube-rs is less mature than Go's controller-runtime.

Add OpenTelemetry trace correlation across gateway activity
Enterprise Observability
feat(server): metrics instrumentation
feat(observability): investigate portable sandbox log collection

detected_features.summary: OpenShell has OCSF structured security logging and anonymous telemetry but zero OpenTelemetry integration. No span injection in gRPC handlers, no trace correlation across gateway-supervisor communication, no OTLP export. The opentelemetry-rust crate is mature and integrates well with the tracing crate OpenShell already uses. This is the highest-feasibility, most-independent candidate — clean addition with no architectural disruption.

openshell_issues.title: Enterprise Observability
feat(server): metrics instrumentation
Managed inference gateway returns 200 with content:null on token exhaustion

detected_features.summary: OpenShell's Privacy Router handles inference routing and credential injection but has zero token tracking, cost accounting, or budget enforcement. Kagenti's LLM Budget Proxy is a clean, self-contained FastAPI proxy that can be ported as middleware in the openshell-router crate. The existing inference proxy path makes this a natural extension point — parse token counts from LLM responses, store in gateway persistence, enforce limits.

Sandbox to Sandbox Communications
multi-player use cases

detected_features.summary: OpenShell has no concept of sessions beyond SSH sessions and sandbox lifecycle. There is no conversation persistence, no message history, and no session trees. Kagenti's session system stores conversation history in PostgreSQL with parent/child delegation relationships. This can be ported as a new proto message type and object type in OpenShell's existing persistence layer.

detected_features.summary: OpenShell consumes SPIFFE via dynamic token grants but does not natively deploy or manage SPIRE. Kagenti deploys SPIRE server/agent via Helm with CSI driver for automatic SVID mounting. The Helm chart has nascent SPIRE CI values. Extending the chart with SPIRE subchart integration and adding SVID-to-sandbox-identity mapping would close the gap.

detected_features.summary: OpenShell sandboxes are completely isolated from each other by design. There is no sandbox-to-sandbox communication, no agent discovery, no multi-agent orchestration, and no A2A protocol. Kagenti has A2A protocol support and DynamicAgentRequest for spawning child agents. This fundamentally changes OpenShell's isolation model and is very high complexity.

embed agentgateway in openshell-sandbox for inference + MCP

detected_features.summary: OpenShell has excellent MCP policy enforcement at the L7 proxy but no MCP routing gateway. The sandbox proxy enforces which MCP calls are allowed but there is no centralized gateway that discovers, registers, and routes to multiple MCP servers. Kagenti uses an Envoy-based MCP gateway with MCPServerRegistration CRDs.

detected_features.summary: OpenShell can perform OAuth2 token grants via SPIFFE JWTs but has no RFC 8693 token exchange for delegation chains (user → sandbox → tool audience scoping). The proxy does credential injection but not audience-scoped token exchange. Multiple issues track generalizing brokered credential delivery.

Multi-tenant deployments
Kubernetes Operator
Support platform-managed K8s sandboxes with namespace, Secret, and SandboxClaim controls

detected_features.summary: OpenShell has strong per-sandbox policy but no fleet-wide hierarchical access control. Gateway-global policy can override sandbox-scoped policy (two tiers) but there is no namespace/component/developer tier hierarchy. OIDC role policy is still being developed. Kagenti implements a four-tier model with Cortex sidecar, OPA PDP, and XACML alignment.
